name: as-any
description: `as any` erases the type checker at that expression — on money and multi-tenant paths that's where a mispriced charge or a cross-org data leak hides. `(req as any)` and `(req.user as any).id`-style casts have typed replacements (AuthenticatedRequest + req.user.id, getOrganizationId(req)); Express-internals monkey-patches are the residual baseline. This ratchet freezes the count and drives it strictly DOWN — lower baselineCount whenever a reduction lands.
lastBumpNote: 1429 -> 1428 on 2026-07-29: platform money-custody purge (founder ruling "be the rail, not the provider"). marketplace.completeTransaction() carried `.set({ stripePaymentIntentId: paymentIntent.id } as any)` against a column that does not exist on marketplace_transactions, inside a swallowing catch — so Drizzle would have thrown and the id was NEVER persisted while the code read as if it were. The cast was the only thing hiding it. Replaced with an honest structured log line (the Stripe side already carries metadata.transactionId); the frozen marketplace module does not get a new column for it. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1433 -> 1429 on 2026-07-29: Wave B ('Wire the engine') cleanup. The wave's 7 new casts were TYPED rather than baselined — leads.deletedAt/organizationId read straight off the Lead row (organizationId is notNull, so the old `as number | undefined` was actively lying about a multi-tenant key), the CSV-import drizzle insert and the workflow_delay_resume claim-update payloads type-check as-is, isWithinQuietHoursForLead accepts a Lead unchanged, and the two contactFrequency boundaries were narrowed to precise shapes (`Record<string, unknown>` for the organizations.settings jsonb blob; `Date | string | null` for the driver-dependent timestamp) per the routes-rent-ledger.ts precedent. Fixing the underlying types also cleared 3 pre-existing casts of the same shape in sequenceProcessor.ts. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule.
